Get or set package options

Source: R/core-registry-options.R
hr_options.Rd

hr_options() with no arguments returns the full option list. Called with a single string it returns that option. Called with name = value pairs it sets them and invisibly returns the previous values, so it composes with on.exit().

Usage

hr_options(...)

Arguments

...

Nothing, a single option name, name = value pairs, or a named list (the form hr_options() itself returns, so a saved value can be restored directly).

Value

The option list, a single option value, or (when setting) the old values invisibly.

Details

Options are read at call time, never captured at load time, so changing an option mid-session affects subsequent runs.

Options

verbose (TRUE)

Print a line for each ingest, segment and read stage. In an interactive session, also keep one line up to date with how many chunks a long read has done and what the run has spent.

model ("gpt-5.6-terra")

Default chat model. Note the default is a reasoning model, which does not accept temperature.

embedding_model ("text-embedding-3-small")

Default embedding model.

tokenizer ("heuristic")

Token counter: "heuristic" (conservative, no dependencies), "words", "chars", "tiktoken" (needs reticulate), or a name registered via hr_set_tokenizer().

api ("responses")

"responses" or "chat" request shape.

api_base ("https://api.openai.com/v1")

API root; point this at a proxy or a compatible endpoint.

api_headers (none)

Named character vector of extra HTTP headers sent with every request, for gateways that do not authenticate with a bearer token. Inherited by every hr_client() that does not name its own; see that function's headers argument for the rules.

temperature (NULL)

Default sampling temperature. NULL omits the field. Dropped automatically for models that reject it. Untested: NULL sends no temperature, so the model decides.

max_retries (4)

Retries for transient failures. HTTP 400 is never retried: a malformed request stays malformed. Untested: set when retries were written, with no measurement behind the number.

retry_pause_base (2)

Seconds; exponential backoff base. Untested: set when retries were written.

request_timeout (120)

Per-request timeout, seconds. Untested: set when the HTTP client was written.

safety_margin (0.10)

Fraction of the context window left unused to absorb tokenizer error. Not a spending cap (see max_cost_usd). Untested: set to absorb the error of counting tokens locally, and not measured against it.

min_output_tokens (256)

Floor on the completion room hr_budget() reserves when reserve_output is not given explicitly. An explicit reserve_output is used between 1 token and the model's max_output, unless it leaves no input room; then it drops to this floor, as the default reserve does. Untested: set as a floor for a short reply.

cache_documents (TRUE)

Cache ingestion per file + settings. The key covers file size, mtime and every option that changes the output.

cache_embeddings (TRUE)

Cache embeddings per text + model.

embedder (NULL)

Which registered embedder to use. NULL means the one the client carries, if any, and otherwise "api". Naming one here overrides both. See gr_embedders(); recording a run with a deterministic embedder is what lets an hr_replay_client() reproduce its chunk ranking.

cache_dir (NULL)

Directory hr_cache() stores model responses in. NULL means a per-session directory under tempdir(), which costs nothing and disappears with the session. Set it to a real path, such as tools::R_user_dir("harnessr", "cache"), to keep responses across sessions and make a long run resumable.

parallel (FALSE)

Run per-chunk calls concurrently. Needs the future and future.apply packages; without them it warns and runs sequentially.

workers (4)

Worker processes when parallel is TRUE. Untested: set when parallel runs were added. It does not change output.

max_cost_usd (5)

Spending limit per run, in USD. A run whose reader sends every chunk is refused before it starts when sending them would cost more than this. Every request is then checked before it is sent, against what the run has spent plus the most the request could cost (its prompt, and its reply at the output cap), and one that could pass the limit is not sent (see hr_governor()), so a run ends at or under the limit with a partial answer. With parallel = TRUE a reader that sends batches is also refused before it starts when its worst case, every reply at its token cap and the price of the dearest model it uses, would pass the limit, and each worker is held to its share of what is left. A chat model with no registered price (see hr_models()) is not held by the limit: its requests are sent with a warning, unless allow_unpriced is FALSE. Under a limit of 0 a model registered at no cost runs and one with a price is refused. NULL removes the limit.

max_calls (400)

Hard cap on model calls per run, checked before every request. A request to an embeddings endpoint (the built-in "api" embedder) counts as one, and is checked and priced against max_cost_usd the same way; an embedding served from the session cache is free. A request an hr_cache() answers counts. NULL removes the cap.

max_tokens_total (NULL)

Most tokens one run may use: the prompt and reply tokens of every call, cache hits included, and the text sent to be embedded. A request is refused when what the run has used plus its prompt and its reply at the cap would pass it. The limit that still bounds a run on a model with no price. NULL for no limit.

max_output_tokens (NULL)

The largest output cap one request may be sent with. A request with a larger cap (for a reasoning model, the raised cap hr_call() sends) is refused rather than cut down. NULL for no ceiling.

allowed_models (NULL)

Character vector of the model ids a run may call, chat and embedding models alike. A request to any other is refused. NULL for any model.

allow_unpriced (TRUE)

Whether a chat model with no registered price may be called while max_cost_usd is set. On, such a request is sent, its cost is recorded as unknown (NA), and the first request to each such model in a session warns with class hr_unpriced_model. Off, it is refused with a condition of that class. Untested: harnessr ships no prices, so off would refuse every built-in model until you set its prices with hr_register_model() or hr_load_models().

reserve_calls (0)

Calls held back from max_calls for a run's closing requests, such as a reader's final answer. An ordinary request is refused once it would reach into them; a request sent with hr_call(closing = TRUE) may use them (see hr_governor()). 0 holds none back. A value above max_calls is refused with class hr_bad_reserve, both here and in hr_governor(). Untested: a choice, not a tuned value.

reserve_usd (0)

Dollars held back from max_cost_usd for a run's closing requests, in the same way. 0 holds none back. A value above max_cost_usd is refused with class hr_bad_reserve. Untested: a choice, not a tuned value.

on_overflow ("error")

What a request does when the provider refuses its prompt as longer than the model's context window (an error of class hr_context_overflow; see hr_call()). "error" returns the failed result. A function of (messages, info) is called with the messages sent and a list of label, model, estimate_tokens (the local count of the prompt), context_window and error, and returns smaller messages, which are sent once more as a new request: the governor checks it, the trace records it as a step with overflow_retry = TRUE, and it is not retried again. Return NULL to send nothing more. Write the function yourself, and keep it deterministic, such as one that cuts the longest message with hr_truncate(); harnessr never asks a model to shorten a prompt. Untested: a choice, not a tuned value.

command_hide_env (none)

More variables to hide from the programs hr_step_command() runs: a character vector of regular expressions matched against variable names, without regard to case, such as "^MY_GATEWAY$". Added to the built-in list, which hides names ending in _API_KEY, _TOKEN, _SECRET, _PASSWORD, _PAT or _SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, the common provider variables, and variables whose value is one of the api_headers values, or the key set with options(harnessr.api_key =), of 8 characters or more (see "Credentials" in hr_step_command()). Untested: a choice.

command_temp_home (FALSE)

Whether hr_step_command() runs its program with HOME (and USERPROFILE on Windows) set to an empty folder made for the call, so it does not read your configuration files and stored logins. Untested: a choice.

mask_secrets (FALSE)

Whether key-shaped strings are replaced with <masked> in the copies harnessr stores or shows: the output a command step keeps, the file hr_trace_save() writes, and a printed trace. Turn it on before you share a trace or a step's output, since an HTTP error body or a program's output can echo a key. The shapes masked are OpenAI and Anthropic keys (sk-...), GitHub tokens (ghp_..., github_pat_...), AWS access key ids (AKIA...), Google API keys (AIza...), Slack tokens (xox...), Hugging Face tokens (hf_...), JSON web tokens and the token after Bearer . In a command step's output the values of the variables the step hides are masked too; in a saved or printed trace only the shapes are. The trace records how many were masked: masked in a command step's note and at the top of a saved trace, and a masked: line in the print. The trace in your session, the cache and every cache and replay key keep the text as it was. A command step passes its masked output on in $check, so a later step that builds a prompt from it sends the masked text, under another cache key. Off, nothing is masked and every copy is byte for byte what it was. Untested: a choice.

price_max_age_days (120)

How old a price may be, in days, before a cost computed from it warns with class hr_stale_price. A price's age is counted from the first day of its as_of month (see hr_models()), and the warning is given once per model per session. Built-in models have no prices, so it applies to prices you set. NULL turns the warning off. Untested: about four months, so prices set once are checked again a few times a year.

unknown_model_action ("warn")

"warn" or "error" when a model id is not in the registry.

actor (none)

A named list (or character vector) of the actor fields every hr_trace() records: system, owner, run_by, purpose and approved_by, each one string. A field named here is recorded on each new trace unless hr_trace() is given its own; one named nowhere is NA. Other names are refused with an error of class gr_bad_option.

auto_max_tokens (50000)

The largest document, in tokens, that answer_document() with recipe = "auto" reads with "fast" (one request); a larger one is read with "thorough". Untested: the value is about 70 pages of prose and under a twentieth of the default model's window, and nothing has measured where the two recipes' answers diverge.

auto_room_share (0.5)

The second condition of that choice: the document must fill at most this share of the input room hr_budget() leaves on every model of the run. Untested: the other half was left for the error of counting tokens locally.

reasoning_floor (2048)

The smallest output cap a request to a reasoning model is sent with. A smaller cap is raised to it, within the model's limit and the room the context window leaves, so a short structured call is not used up by reasoning; 0 turns the raise off. The trace's params_sent records the cap sent. Untested: a reasoning model can spend a few hundred to a couple of thousand tokens before it replies, and the value was not measured. A value other than the default joins the response-cache key and the store key of gr_read_many().

output_reserve_share (0.25)

The share of the usable window hr_budget() reserves for the reply when no reserve_output is given, between min_output_tokens and the model's output limit. It sets the input room of such a budget. The readers give max_answer_tokens as the reserve, so it does not change how much of a document they fit in one request. Untested.

near_verbatim_sim (0.90), near_verbatim_sim_short (0.95), near_verbatim_short_chars (40)

The least similarity a quotation of at least near_verbatim_short_chars characters (after normalising), and one shorter than that, needs for the edit-distance matcher to score it near_verbatim (see gr_verify_evidence()). The values come from practitioner sources and were not tuned; the matcher's error rates at them were measured on a labelled set of 343 true and 162 false quotations (see NEWS). The status is recorded only, unless accept_near_verbatim = TRUE (see gr_read_spec()). A value other than the default joins the store key of gr_read_many().

Where the defaults come from

The settings listed last above were constants in the code until they were options; each keeps the constant's value. A trace records them, and price_max_age_days, reserve_calls, reserve_usd, on_overflow, command_hide_env, command_temp_home and mask_secrets, (in its options snapshot) only when one is not its default, so a trace made at the defaults reads as it did before they existed. A function given as on_overflow is recorded as "<function>". Each tuning setting's entry above (temperature, max_retries, retry_pause_base, request_timeout, safety_margin, min_output_tokens, workers, price_max_age_days and the settings listed last) says where its default came from, as do those of allow_unpriced, the reserves, on_overflow and the three credential settings; "untested" means no measurement backs the value. The other entries are switches, limits and names, which are choices rather than tuned values.

Checked values

Numeric options are checked when they are set, and the two kinds are treated differently because a wrong value costs different things.

The ceilings, max_cost_usd, max_calls, max_tokens_total and max_output_tokens, refuse anything that is not a single number of zero or more (one or more for max_output_tokens), with an error of class gr_bad_option: a limit that cannot be compared is not a limit, and ignoring it spends money. NULL and Inf both mean "no limit". allowed_models must be NULL or a character vector of ids, and allow_unpriced TRUE or FALSE. The reserves, reserve_calls and reserve_usd, must be a single finite number of 0 or more, and are refused otherwise with the same class; reserve_calls is rounded down. A reserve larger than its limit, as the two stand once every setting of the call is in, is refused with classes hr_bad_reserve and gr_bad_option, and the call changes nothing.

The tuning settings (safety_margin [0, 0.5], min_output_tokens [0, 1e6], max_retries [0, 10], retry_pause_base [0, 60], request_timeout [1, 3600], workers [1, 32], temperature [0, 2], auto_max_tokens [0, 1e7], auto_room_share [0, 1], reasoning_floor [0, 1e6], output_reserve_share [0, 0.9], near_verbatim_sim and near_verbatim_sim_short [0, 1], near_verbatim_short_chars [0, 1e4] and price_max_age_days [0, 3650]) read a number written as text as that number. A value they cannot read, such as NA or "x", warns (gr_bad_option) and leaves the current setting unchanged; a value outside the range is clamped into it, with the same warning. Whole-number settings are rounded down. temperature also takes NULL, its default, and price_max_age_days takes NULL to turn its warning off.

See also

hr_register_model() to correct a model's limits, hr_set_tokenizer(), hr_budget(), hr_cache()

Examples

old <- hr_options(verbose = FALSE)
hr_options("verbose")
#> [1] FALSE
hr_options(old)
